questions.question: Explain the difference between a 2D shape and a 3D object, using a circle and a ball as examples, and explain what a face is.
questions.expected_answer: A 2D shape is flat with only length and width, like a circle drawn on paper. A 3D object takes up space with length, width and height, like a ball. A face is a flat surface of a 3D object, and each face is itself a 2D shape, such as the rectangular faces of a box.

questions.question: Describe a rectangular prism and a cylinder by their faces, edges, vertices and curved surfaces, and give an everyday example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices, like a cereal box. A cylinder has 2 circular faces, 1 curved surface and no vertices, like a tin of beans.

questions.question: Describe a sphere and a square pyramid, and give the four questions that would let you name any of the four objects in this topic.
questions.expected_answer: A sphere has one curved surface and no faces, edges or vertices, like a soccer ball. A square pyramid has 1 square base and 4 triangular faces meeting at an apex, 5 faces in all. Questions: curved all over means sphere; two circles and a curved side means cylinder; six rectangular faces means rectangular prism; a base with triangles meeting at a point means pyramid.
